Protocol: `docs/09_benchmark.md`.

Rows are **zero-shot** (no adaptation) and slide windows over the span(s) named above — for zero-shot rows the whole series is legitimate because the model saw no training data; an *adapted* checkpoint must be scored with `--spans test`, or the comparison leaks. Same horizon grid, same window count, same seed for every model. Rows carry the **registry key the sweep requested** (adapters may report a family-level key internally). `ctx` is the context actually used (an oversized one is clamped to the span, which is recorded, not hidden). **CRPS/WQL/pinball appear only for models that emit quantiles**; a point-only model gets point metrics and is marked `pt` — a probabilistic column with a dash is not a zero. `skill` is `1 − MASE` (MASE normalises by the in-sample mean |Δ| of the train span), so MASE is the column to read and a negative skill means the model lost to that trivial scaler on this series. `cov@80` is empirical coverage of the nominal 80% band (`nominal_80` in the JSON rows carries the nominal value the model actually claims, which is not always exactly 0.8 for models with their own quantile grid).

## Headline ranking

`beat naive` is the share of cells where the model's MASE beats the **naive row scored on the same (series, span, horizon) cell** - not MASE < 1: MASE's denominator is the in-sample mean |delta| of the train span, so on these series naive itself sits near 4.5 and a MASE < 1 test calls everything a loss. The ratio column is the median of per-cell `mase_model / mase_naive`, which is comparable across data paths (same bytes, same split, same denominator on both sides); raw median MASE is scoped to this pass. `ctx` prints the context lengths actually used - different ctx is a different measurement. `no measurement` counts cells whose windows were all non-finite or unscored; those never enter a median.

## Repeated cell keys: 404

These `(model, series, span, horizon)` keys were measured more than once in the merge inputs; the table keeps the newest. Classifying every measurement pair by protocol signature (ctx, ctx_note, device, code_sha, torch): **808** pairs sit under a *different* signature - an earlier measurement superseded by a fix, where the gap is the size of that fix - and **0** share a signature, so their gap is run variance.

Superseded by a protocol change: ttm-r2 (404), ttm-r3 (404)

Gap between a superseded cell and the one that replaced it: median 0.00%, max 11047.6%. Some of these only differ by a code sha (gap ~0.0002%) and are plain re-runs; the large ones are a protocol fix, which is why the number is quoted and not averaged away.

Quote a model's ranking only where its gap to the next model exceeds the run-variance spread above.
